$comment: Advisories against a pinned engine that do not reach ShellPilot, each with the
reason it does not. Read by scripts/check-engine-advisories.mjs.
A suppression is a judgement made on a day about one version, so it carries both.
It stops applying when the pin moves (appliesToVersion) or when the reasoning ages
out (reviewBy), and in either case the CVE becomes a finding again rather than
passing quietly. Suppressions are matched by exact CVE id, so a newly published
advisory is never covered by an existing entry.
Suppress reachability, never severity. 'Low score' is not a reason; 'the code is

suppressions.reason: affects ovpn-dco-win, which we neither compile nor ship
detail: A heap overflow in the epoch key generator of ovpn-dco-win, OpenVPN's
data-channel-offload kernel driver for Windows. NVD records it against the
cpe:2.3:a:openvpn:openvpn range 2.0.0 to 2.8.3, which is why it matches our
pin, but the affected code is the separate Windows driver rather than the
Two independent reasons it cannot reach a ShellPilot user. The build passes
--disable-dco (scripts/build-openvpn.sh), so no DCO code is compiled into the
binary we ship. And we ship no OpenVPN binary on Windows at all: Windows keeps
the system-install requirement, so its openvpn comes from the OpenVPN
installer and is that project's to patch, not ours.
Either alone would be sufficient. Both hold.
